newsitem.title: USA: Apple outlines new product road map-report.
newsitem.headline: Apple outlines new product road map-report.

text.p: Apple Computer Inc plans an aggressive roll-out of new products in the next year, ranging from $800 computing devices and low-priced Macs to powerful servers and a PC microprocessor capable of running at 500 megahertz, according to a newspaper report.

The San Jose Mercury News Thursday reported that Marco Landi, Apple executive vice president and chief operating officer, described a product road map that includes a Mac priced at less than $1,700, a server computer capable of running multiple operating systems, a 500 megahertz PowerPC chip, new laptops and a $800 device for schoolchildren.
Apple officials would not respond to telephone inquiries about the products described in the report.
Analysts said the list of product introductions in the report was noteworthy for Landi's willingness to specify prices and delivery dates.

"This indicates to me that Marco feels confident enough about Apple's current manufacturing, forecasting, reliability and quality control, service and support - the whole infrastructure - that he is willing to do what I and others have been asking him to and put some stakes in the ground as to when they'll deliver and at what price," said analyst Pieter Hartsook, who follows the Apple Macintosh markets and publishes the Hartsook Letter.

"Apple historically has had problems in forecasting, manufacturing, quality control, marketing - this whole legacy of not being able to get things to market that's troubled them for the last 12 months," Hartsook said.
"All of them are likely to make a difference to Apple's prospects. But dating something and doing something are two entirely different things," he added.

Montgomery Securities analyst Kurt King said Apple's reported plan to offer a Mac for less than $1,700 is the most interesting because the company needs to return to the home computer market with an affordable PC.
